verification_report.summary:
The supplied dual supplement is correct under the expressly accepted inputs. Fifteen sequential statement checks and three reference/dependency checks found no critical errors or gaps. The chapter was read for the exact scalar, ordinary-type, envelope and support definitions; the audit was confined to the supplement and the book source was left unchanged.

The continuous-test supremum is convex, weakly lower semicontinuous and bounded below by finite B_phi(0), so it never takes the value -infinity. Equality in the dual inequality is exactly the existing supporting-probability inequality, with the correct sign. Nonempty continuous support sets therefore give finite attained minima and the precise minimizer characterization.

For every finite dual sublevel, bounded-L1 continuity at each fixed t yields the required cutoff modulus. The cutoff estimate is uniform over all measures in the sublevel. Outer and inner regularity extend it to Borel sets, and the epsilon/2 margin preserves the strict supremum bound. This proves absolute continuity and, together with probability normalization, uniform integrability. Uniform approximation of bounded measurable tests then upgrades narrow convergence within the sublevel to weak L1 convergence. Compact metrizability of X supplies convergent measure subsequences, establishing the asserted weak-L1 sequential compactness without an additional compactness theorem.

The measurable extension respects L-infinity equivalence classes. Finite dual value implies absolute continuity before measurable integration is used. Bounded continuous approximation proves the measurable-test supremum identity for such measures. The declared infinite objective for every infinite-dual measure avoids undefined integrals against measures charging volume-null sets. Approximating supports lie in the single sublevel H_phi<=B_phi(0)+2M. Uniform absolute continuity controls the varying integrals of F_j-F, and lower semicontinuity establishes finite dual value at the limit before the measurable supremum identity is invoked. This proves existence, exact agreement with continuous supports, stability of every weak-L1 cluster point, and full weak-L1 convergence when the limiting support set is a singleton.

The accepted closed-case mass input uses ordinary equivalence by bounded additive comparisons. SGPT Definition 1.5.2, Proposition 2.2.2 and Theorem 2.4.3 match this context; mass invariance follows by applying monotonicity in both directions. The required arXiv theorem search was followed by web fallback and direct reading of the supplied SGPT manuscript, with corroboration in [Witt Nystrom, Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950). Positivity also follows from the accepted equation at F=0. Integration gives the stated B_phi formula, and differentiation in bounded directions with both parameter signs identifies the unique exponential supporting probability.

The entropy identity is valid for nonnormalized dV, zeros of the density, infinite entropy, and every measure that is not absolutely continuous, including mixtures with a singular component. The negative part of h log h is integrable. Jensen applies in the finite-entropy case. For the reverse bound, the clipped densities converge in L1, the positive parts of h F_k increase, and their negative parts are dominated by the integrable negative part of h log h. Continuous approximation at each fixed k is valid even when H_phi is infinite, so the argument is not circular. There is no missing volume constant: entropy is bounded below by -log dV(X), with equality at normalized dV; negative entropy can occur when dV(X)>1.

For continuous real a, the equivalent reference measure e^a dV has the same null sets. Its equation is already the original equation with logarithmic density F+a, so smoothness of a and a new PDE existence theorem are unnecessary. Translation by a preserves C(X), giving H'_phi=H_phi-integral a dnu. The subtracted integral is finite for every probability, so the identity remains valid at +infinity. No fixed-mass entropy computation is extended to general nonclosed backgrounds. All geometric assumptions enter through the accepted normalization inputs; no BMP, uniform positive lower mass, new global nonlinear PDE, common Lp bound for p>1, strong L1 convergence, or unconditional uniqueness is used or claimed.
